title: DeploymentManifest
description: Output of data-deploy. Turns a data-pipeline pipeline-manifest.json whose modality_decision.chosen is lakeflow_connect and readiness_level is approved_for_deployment into real Databricks Asset Bundle resources (a Unity Catalog connection definition and an ingestion-pipeline/destination resource) plus a Lakeflow Connect connector-type resolution -- NOT the generated resource files themselves, which live on disk under output_dir, same split as pipeline-manifest.json vs. its generated code. data-deploy never runs `databricks bundle deploy`, creates a live connector, or otherwise touches a client workspace; a second, separate human approval (this schema's own deployment field, distinct from approval_gate below) is required before that, and even then this skill only records it -- see skills/data-deploy/references/approval-gate.md and references/toolkit-conventions.md #7.

deployment_id.description: Stable identifier across re-runs for the same source pipeline_id, so a new run's diff can be matched to a previous one.

source_pipeline_manifest_ref.description: The pipeline-manifest.json this deployment manifest was built from. data-deploy never generates bundle resources with no upstream pipeline manifest.

approval_gate.description: Echoes the source pipeline-manifest's OWN recorded approval (its `deployment` field) that licensed this run to act at all -- data-deploy does not re-decide or re-collect this approval, it only refuses to run without one already present naming a target. See skills/data-deploy/references/approval-gate.md for why this is a distinct gate from this schema's own `deployment` field below.

source_target_named.description: Echoed verbatim from the source pipeline-manifest's deployment.target_named.

targets.description: One entry per target table in the source pipeline-manifest. Only the one named in approval_gate.source_target_named is actually processed (skipped: false); every other target present in the source manifest still gets an entry here with skipped: true, so a table silently being left out is never mistaken for it having been handled -- see references/approval-gate.md.

skipped_reason.description: Required (non-null) when skipped is true -- e.g. 'not named in the source pipeline-manifest's deployment.target_named'.

source_system.description: Named explicitly by the invoking agent (never parsed/guessed from the data-contract's source.object naming convention, which is not consistent across source systems -- see references/connector-type-mapping.md), then resolved deterministically to connector_type by scripts/resolve_connector_type.py.

connector_type.description: The Lakeflow Connect connector type identifier resolved from source_system, e.g. 'SQLSERVER', 'SALESFORCE'.

connection_name.description: Name of the Unity Catalog connection this target's ingestion pipeline depends on. A connection is typically shared across many pipelines/tables from the same source system, not created per target -- see references/asset-bundle-resources.md.

unsupported_source_systems.description: source_system values named for a target that scripts/resolve_connector_type.py did not recognize -- refused, never guessed at a plausible-looking connector_type. Never silently dropped; see references/connector-type-mapping.md for the supported list and how to extend it.

readiness_level.description: draft: bundle resources rendered but not sanity-checked. validated: every processed target's generated_files exist on disk and are structurally valid YAML with no unresolved placeholders. approved_for_deployment: a human has explicitly approved, in this conversation, actually running `databricks bundle deploy` (or creating the connector) against a named target -- see `deployment` below. deployed: set by whatever actually deployed, never by this skill.

deployment.description: A SECOND, separate human approval from approval_gate above -- that one licensed generating these bundle resources; this one licenses actually running `databricks bundle deploy` or creating a live connector, which data-deploy never does itself. Null until a human explicitly approves, in-conversation, naming the specific target. See references/approval-gate.md.

target_named.description: The specific target job/object/connection name the human approval named -- never a blanket approval.
